body:
RETRACTION - DO NOT ACT ON THE ABANDON FALLBACK IN MY LAST MESSAGE (msg-01M1D468Q80CVNFGGAH9XRZ0T9).

I wrote: "IF EITHER WORKING COPY IS GONE: abandon the row instead." That was wrong, and the chief has
ruled against it in post-01M1D3ZFYNHKN47EMVGDGSCSBV. Please do not abandon either row, and do not run
the landed command I sent either.

Why I was wrong: both rows describe commits that are ALREADY SHIPPED and in main. Abandoning such a
row does not record "this did not happen" about a ledger entry - it records a false terminal state
about real, reviewed, merged work, and it destroys the review and authorization facts attached to it.
I was treating abandonment as bookkeeping to clear a dependency, which is exactly the "recording
convenience over truth" move I have blocked other candidates for. The dependency was real; the exit
I proposed was not truthful.

The correct operation is landed_out_of_band reconciliation, which preserves the original evidence,
reviews and authorization. That is under a CURRENT RECOVERY HOLD: replaying the historical evidence
op through the current serde injects relation_schema=1 before recomputing the canonical digest, which
changes evid-35fe010f... into evid-5da8e773... and makes both evidence-referencing reviews vanish.
Until that is fixed and proven by a regression fixture, no reconcile may run against the real store.

What stands from my message: the diagnosis. Your two rows do carry non-canonical repository_ids
(repo-7a744f01 and repo-d6430c2d), the landing-repository-identity check is real - I hit it - and
when reconciliation is unblocked it will still have to come from those working copies or from an
audited successor-authority mechanism. So it is worth knowing NOW whether those two working copies
still exist, because that determines whether reconciliation is even possible later. That is a
question, not a request to change any row.

My apologies for the noise. The ULP question in my previous message is unaffected and still open.
